chunks: And from Sa'd, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'labah, from Mubarak al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: By the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), there are four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, weeping for him until the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: How many angels weep for Imam Husayn at his grave?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) declaration that four thousand angels, described as disheveled and dust-covered, weep by Imam Husayn’s (a.s.) grave until the Day of Judgment. This tradition underscores the cosmic scale of the Ashura tragedy, illustrating how the martyrdom of the Ahl al-Bayt resonates eternally in the celestial realm, serving as a perpetual sign of divine grief and validation for Shia devotees.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain both narrated to me from Sa’d (ibn ‘Abdillāh), from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Ibn Faďďāl, from Tha’labah, from Mubārak Al-‘Aťťār, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said to me: There are four thousand angels by the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) who are disheveled and covered with dust; they cry over him (and will continue to do so) until the Day of Judgment.
